stories.story: As the project owner I want the Code reviewed against each Contract spec so that I know where the Code does not implement what the Contracts define.
acceptance: Every bus covered by the Contracts (CAN, SPI, HOST, TIME) is checked against the Code

stories.story: As the maintainer I want one latest-value store that accepts samples and feedback, ages them against their freshness windows and hands out a coherent copy, so that the snapshot coherency promise (SPI_SYSTEM_INTERFACE §8), the stale record and the R15 protection each have one owner and one test surface. acceptance: New module Arm_Sensor_Hub/App/{Inc,Src}/latest_value.[ch] (prefix LatestValue_; records LatestValue_SensorRecord, LatestValue_MotorRecord) replaces sensor_latest_value and motor_latest_value; added to both CMake source lists

Interface is four calls and nothing else: Configure (per-axis fitted flag; registered motors as index plus axis, from the app_init commissioning tables), AcceptSample (axis, raw counts, magnet status, acquisition timestamp), AcceptFeedback (motor, typed position or speed or drive status, acquisition timestamp), CopySnapshot (now, caller-provided buffer). No single-record reader until a second caller exists

Not fitted and not registered are slot properties set by Configure; a write to such a slot returns an error. The sensor task no longer writes NOT_FITTED and the SPI service no longer filters motor records by joint id

Freshness is decided by the store at CopySnapshot: stale when now minus acquisition timestamp exceeds the kind's window. Motor window PRM-MOT-01. New register row, Provisional: sensor freshness window = 5 × PRM-ACQ-05 (100 ms), basis Derived from PRM-ACQ-05, to be Measured in Stage 3. Producers no longer mark stale; a decode error stays an error counter in the CAN service
Escalation per PRM-MOT-02 (degraded, inhibit, FAULT) stays in the CAN service, derived from the age the store reports

Typed feedback is merged in the store with per-field timestamps; the record is valid once a position has arrived and its acquisition timestamp is the position's; speed has its own validity flag. The raw last 31H position reply and its command code are kept alongside (R10(a), B83) only so the schema v1 motor record stays byte-identical, and are removed with schema v2

stories.title: S9.14 Exchange owner on the Pi: ExchangeSession with transact and exchange, one firmware-rules fake, process-wide Sequencer
stories.story: As the maintainer I want one module that sends a request, clocks the transaction, correlates the reply that arrives in a later transaction and paces the link, returning one record per transaction, so that the harness, the probes, the snapshot logger and ClockSync all consume one record type instead of four hand-rolled loops and five unshared fakes. Architecture review 2026-10-15, candidate 3 (Strong); design settled with Lenton Neale the same day (size: 3 points).
acceptance: RaspberryPi_Sensor_Hub/src/spi/exchange.py holds ExchangeSession, grown from timing.TimingSession (TransactionRecord keeps its name and CSV fields); spi_device.py and SpiDevice are deleted

Interface is two calls: transact(request) paces (DataReadyLike or min interval), clocks one transaction, records phase timings, decodes, correlates against the pending table and returns one TransactionRecord; exchange(request, filler=GET_STATUS, budget) transacts the request then filler until its reply correlates, a NACK correlates, or the budget is spent

exchange returns a result object with outcome (replied, refused, exhausted), the reply frame or the NACK status and detail, and the records consumed; firmware outcomes never raise. Bus and decode errors stay exceptions. Message-specific helpers (version read for the evidence tool) are functions over exchange in their callers, not methods
The pending table makes the session a stream: any transaction may carry any request and every reply correlates to whichever pending request it answers; exchange is the stop-and-wait special case

TransactionRecord gains the observation fields (Pi send time, request_received_local_us when present, Pi receive time) so B94's ClockSync is fed from records by its owner; the session has no dependency on ClockSync. It gains the raw response bytes when decoding fails, absent otherwise

Sequences come from a process-wide Sequencer in spi_protocol.py beside initial_sequence(), injected into ExchangeSession with a shared default; R3's single bounded jump on BAD_SEQUENCE (B69) lives there. Two sessions in one process never both start from the seed

src/spi/fake_backend.py is one SpiBackend adapter enforcing the firmware's rules: one-transaction reply delay, sequence high-water mark with BAD_SEQUENCE, BAD_STATE before activation, VERSION and SNAPSHOT replies from configured records, CRC check of the request, a garbage mode. The five fakes in tests/spi are deleted. spi_link_probe.py and spi_timing_harness.py gain a --fake flag
The fake reproduces the B55 golden vectors byte for byte (test_fake_backend.py), so the C protocol, the Python protocol and the fake are pinned to one set of bytes

Callers migrated: spi_timing_harness.py uses transact and a version-read function over exchange; spi_link_probe.py consumes transact and keeps its verdict logic over the record's raw bytes; spi_time_sync_probe.py is ported to exchange in place (B97 still deletes it)

stories.title: S11.13 Drive protocol module: frame-in feedback-out, per-drive state, poll deadlines, motor ready and the stop sequence; CAN service becomes transport only
stories.story: As the maintainer I want the drive protocol (which drive a frame belongs to, decoding to typed feedback, per-motor poll deadlines and miss counting, motor ready, the controlled-stop state machine) in one pure module with the bxCAN plumbing left in can_service, so that the one module with real behaviour on the motor path is tested frame-in record-out with the real MKS decoder, and B83, B84, B85, B110 and the gate's motor_ready each land in a tested home. Architecture review 2026-10-15, candidate 7; design settled with Lenton Neale the same day (size: 3 points).
acceptance: New module Arm_Sensor_Hub/App/{Inc,Src}/drive_protocol.[ch] (prefix DriveProtocol_), added to both CMake source lists. It takes now in microseconds on every call, reads no clock and drives no lifecycle

DriveProtocol_Init(send, context): one injected send callback with a priority argument (the real seam: can_service enqueue in production, a recording function in tests). DriveProtocol_Register(motor index, axis, model, CAN ID, position and speed feedback periods per R11(b)) from the app_init commissioning tables; app_init registers with this module, not with can_service

DriveProtocol_OnFrame(frame, rx_time): find the registered drive by CAN ID, decode through mks_decode (mks_api.h stays the only byte-layout authority), hand typed feedback straight to the latest-value store (B128): 31H gives position, 32H gives speed and the R22 moving flag; an accepted F3H reply sets motor ready; a reply with status 0 to an enable or motion command clears it

DriveProtocol_Tick(now): emits through send every position or speed read whose per-motor deadline has passed (no shared round-robin); counts a miss when a position deadline passes with no 31H reply since the previous one; escalates per PRM-MOT-02 (one miss degraded, three consecutive FAULT); FAULT clears motor ready; advances each drive's stop state machine

DriveProtocol_Command(motor, kind, params, now): encodes ENABLE, DISABLE, MOVE_TO_POSITION (F5H), MOVE_AT_VELOCITY (F6H) through send and remembers the running motion command per drive. DriveProtocol_Stop(motor, now): starts the R21 sequence in the running command's own stop form (F5H speed 0 after a position move, F6H speed 0 after a velocity move), falls back to F7H when refused or unanswered within the Provisional timeout taken as a parameter; the result (stopped, fell back, failed) is readable. The end state of the sequence follows B110 and, when WP17 amends it, R21

Readable: per-motor ready (R20: registered, ENABLE accepted since the last disable or reset, no drive fault, where drive fault = refused command or feedback FAULT; a drive status query is recorded as open for the bench, not added), per-motor miss state and counters, stop result. The motion gate (B106) reads motor ready here; the health monitor pulls the counters

can_service.[ch] becomes transport only: Init, Activate, GetLifecycleState, Process (drain RX FIFO into OnFrame, call Tick, drain the TX queue, bus-off per B85), Enqueue(frame, priority) as the production send adapter, counters per B87. The eleven command, poll and getter functions in can_service.h are deleted; can_tx_policy stays with the transport

Tests: the real MksServo library (portable C++17, no HAL includes, already a CMake target) is linked into the protocol test executable (C++ enabled for that target in the HostTests preset); frame-in record-out tests there beside the latest-value store tests: 31H updates position, 32H updates speed and moving, refused F3H clears motor ready, three missed deadlines reach FAULT, Stop emits the right form and falls back on timeout, frames and priorities asserted through the recording send. service_test_main.c keeps the B85 plumbing tests and deletes its mks stubs (lines 473-585)

FIRMWARE_ARCHITECTURE.md (currently only on the wp9 branch) lists the module; CAN_SYSTEM_INTERFACE.md names drive_protocol as the implementation of its feedback and command sections in the component documentation
HostTests, the Debug build and the Pi tests pass; doc_check is clean
Depends on S10.15 (B128) and S11.2 (B80); S11.5 (B83), S11.6 (B84), S11.7 (B85) and B110 depend on this story

stories.title: S10.16 SPI response path built once: the protocol module validates, calls one injected handler and writes the frame into the pool's buffer; the service becomes transport
stories.story: As the maintainer I want every Pi-visible response decided and built in one place, spi_protocol.c, from one validation and one handler call, written once into the buffer the frame pool lends, so that the module mirrored by spi_protocol.py holds every message rule, the service holds only lifecycle and DMA, and the messages still to come (DIAGNOSTIC, SET_MOTOR_COMMAND, system-activate) are handler cases rather than service branches. Architecture review 2026-10-15, candidate 4; design settled with Lenton Neale the same day (size: 3 points).
acceptance: SpiProtocol_ProcessRequest(state, request, now_us, receipt_time or none, lent frame buffer): validates framing once (magic, version, length, CRC, sequence, known type, R1 payload rule); advances the request-sequence mark on every frame-valid request whatever the handler answers (R3 compatible); calls the one handler injected at init; writes the complete frame once. The service's separate ValidateRequest call, its own NACK building and the TIME_SYNC override are removed; validation never runs twice

Handler seam: one function injected into SpiProtocol_State at init, handle(request type, request payload, now, out payload region, capacity) returning accepted with length or refused with NACK status and detail. The protocol module lends the handler the frame's payload region and owns everything outside it: header, sequence, frame_time_us from the now parameter, request_received_local_us appended to ACK, VERSION and SNAPSHOT and never to NACK, omitted when the receipt time is absent (R16, B92, B93), CRC. BuildCommandReply and BuildVersionReply become private. Two adapters: the service's static handler and a scripted test handler

The service's handler is the application switch: BAD_STATE when the lifecycle disallows the type; GET_SNAPSHOT serializes a fresh coherent copy from the latest-value store (B128, B65); GET_VERSION; later GET_DIAGNOSTIC (B89), SET_MOTOR_COMMAND with the gate reason (B108), system-activate (B111)

SpiProtocol_StageUnsolicited(kind, payload writer, now): boot and recovery DIAGNOSTIC (R14) and the periodic snapshot (PRM-ACQ-01, zero correlation) through the same private frame builder into a lent buffer. The response path and this call are the only two writers of frames; BuildBootStatus is removed

Buffers: the pool lends its buffer to ProcessRequest and StageUnsolicited through SnapshotBuilder_Stage's callback, so the production serializer writes in place; s_response_frame, SpiProtocol_State.unsolicited_payload and s_pending_request are deleted (about 1.5 KB). s_rx_frame is processed in place; the invariant that DMA is not re-armed while s_request_pending is set is stated beside the flag. The transmit sequence is consumed only for frames that are staged
One source of truth for armed: the pool's SNAPSHOT_FRAME_DMA_ACTIVE state; s_dma_active is deleted (agrees with B66, which keeps the stall and re-arm fixes)

spi_slave_service.h keeps seven entries: Init (period from the register value, no setter), Activate, GetLifecycleState, Process, the two HAL callbacks, GetSnapshotDiagnostics. BeginDmaTransfer, CompleteDmaTransfer, StageSnapshot, StageLatestSnapshot, SetUnsolicitedSnapshot, ProcessRequestFrame, GetDataReadyState and SetPollPeriodMs are removed

Tests in protocol_test_main.c against a scripted handler: each validation failure and its NACK code; the R1 payload rule; the mark advancing on a refused request; receipt time on ACK, VERSION and SNAPSHOT, never NACK, omitted when absent; the unsolicited path; the B55 golden vectors driven through ProcessRequest into a lent buffer. service_test_main.c: the DMA-loop test keeps its intent without the removed exports and asserts the pool state is the only armed flag
FIRMWARE_ARCHITECTURE.md (currently only on the wp9 branch) describes the handler seam; SPI_SYSTEM_INTERFACE.md §4 and §14 are named as implemented by spi_protocol.c in the component documentation
HostTests, the Debug build and the Pi tests pass; doc_check is clean

stories.title: S10.17 AS5600 sample in two transactions: burst reads under one scoped I2C lock, repeated-start write-read, typed magnet condition; driver interface down to InitDevice and ReadSample
stories.story: As the maintainer I want one joint-encoder sample to cost two bus reads instead of fifteen bus transactions, with the timestamp taken right after the angle read and the magnet bits classified in the driver, so that the sweep (PRM-ACQ-02, 46 ms measured) shrinks without touching the task loop and the datasheet knowledge lives in one module. Architecture review 2026-10-15, candidate 6; design settled with Lenton Neale the same day after the datasheet check (size: 2 points).
acceptance: Datasheet basis (icm-project/references/as5600/i2c-interface.md, p. 15 and p. 19 of the local copy): the address pointer increments after each byte except that ANGLE, RAW ANGLE and MAGNITUDE suppress the increment on reads. So a 3-byte read from 0x0B yields STATUS, RAW ANGLE(11:8), RAW ANGLE(7:0) and a 3-byte read from 0x1A yields AGC, MAGNITUDE(11:8), MAGNITUDE(7:0); ANGLE (0x0E) is not reachable in the first burst and, per ruling R6 (B74), is no longer needed because processed_angle_mdeg derives from RAW ANGLE in the latest-value store (B128)

AS5600_ReadSample(dev, sample): take the I2C manager's scoped lock; select the mux channel only if the cached mask differs (the tca9548a cache at tca9548a_mux.c:26-31 is honoured on this path); read 3 bytes at 0x0B; take the acquisition timestamp immediately after that read returns (satisfies B72); read 3 bytes at 0x1A; release the lock. Per axis the bus sees three transactions, four on a cache miss, instead of fifteen

The sample carries raw angle counts, status byte, AGC, magnitude, timestamp and a typed magnet condition (detected, missing, weak, strong) derived from MD, ML, MH in the driver. The angle field is removed. The latest-value store's AcceptSample receives the condition and applies R6 (ML and MH are warnings; SAMPLE_VALID stays set); the sensor task reads and accepts and holds no datasheet bits or record policy

as5600.h shrinks to AS5600_InitDevice, AS5600_ReadSample and the magnet-condition type; ReadStatus, ReadRawAngle, ReadAngle, ReadAgc, ReadMagnitude and RawToDegrees are deleted; bring-up uses ReadSample. The five per-reader TimeService_NowUs calls go with them

I2C manager: a scoped lock (take and release) exposed for the driver's per-axis sequence; the write-read primitive is implemented with HAL_I2C_Mem_Read (pointer write, repeated start, read in one HAL call, the datasheet's p. 19 form) instead of HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit then HAL_I2C_Master_Receive with a STOP between; the manager's interface is otherwise unchanged (this is B73's 'fewer I2C transactions' item made concrete)
AGC and MAGNITUDE are read every sweep; reading them every Nth sweep is a Stage 3 decision taken with a measurement, not here

Tests in service_test_main.c against the HAL stub (which gains HAL_I2C_Mem_Read and a lock counter): per fitted axis the script is lock, mux write only on a cache miss, Mem_Read 3 bytes at 0x0B, Mem_Read 3 bytes at 0x1A, unlock; the timestamp falls between the two reads; a scripted STATUS and RAW ANGLE produce a valid record with the right counts; the existing bring-up, mux-map and not-fitted script tests are updated to the new sequence. In protocol_test_main.c: the store maps each magnet condition to the R6 validity flags
After it lands, PRM-ACQ-02 is re-measured with the sweep counter B74 adds; the row stays Measured with the new date and value, and PRM-ACQ-01 is revisited against it
HostTests, the Debug build and the Pi tests pass; doc_check is clean
Depends on S10.15 (B128); S10.8 (B72) is satisfied by this story; S10.9 (B73) and S10.10 (B74) point at it

stories.title: S9.15 Check the main (interrupt) stack depth at build time
stories.story: As the maintainer I want the main stack (MSP), which every interrupt handler and nested interrupt uses, checked against its worst case after every build, like the task stacks (B53), so that an interrupt-side overflow cannot pass unnoticed. Found in the 2026-10-15 STM32 configuration review.
acceptance: tools/stack_depth.py also checks the main stack: the deepest path of each enabled exception and IRQ handler (from the vector table in startup_stm32f405xx.s and stm32f4xx_it.c), combined across NVIC preemption levels (one handler per level can nest), plus the exception frame each nesting level pushes

The main stack size comes from the linker script (_Min_Stack_Size in STM32F405xx_FLASH.ld); the pre-scheduler path from main() is checked against it too (FreeRTOS resets MSP when the scheduler starts)
Handler priorities are read from the generated code or the .ioc, not restated; a handler whose priority cannot be read fails the check
Function-pointer calls in HAL IRQ handlers (HAL callbacks) are resolved through stack_depth.cfg with site counts, as for tasks
Host tests for the nesting arithmetic; the Debug and Release builds report the main-stack headroom in stack_depth.txt
HostTests, the Debug build and the Pi tests pass; doc_check is clean
